Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned tree appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic thromboembolic disease. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal or only mildly enlarged, making "mild" pulmonary hypertension a more appropriate descriptor than "severe" (which would typically show massive cardiomegaly) or "normal."
